Hi Kimberly,

Quick heads up from MedArc: we are adding two analytics partners (DataWeave Ltd and GeoPulse Inc) to our processing chain to support regional telemetry aggregation for our log analytics pipeline. This will involve forwarding a subset of pseudonymized request metadata and aggregated usage metrics (no raw user prompt text) from our EU ingestion nodes to GeoPulse (US) for enrichment and to DataWeave (IE) for deduplication.

Per our DPA we are providing this notice and seeking your confirmation for onward transfer. We have attached the current vendor roster and a short DPIA summary for the change.

Files attached: medarc_vendor_roster_20261206.csv, medarc_dpia_summary_20261206.pdf

High level:
- What is shared: hashed request IDs, timestamp, model_id, latency buckets, and aggregated counts.
- Retention: telemetry retained 30 days, enrichment results retained 90 days.
- Legal basis: processing under contract; transfers covered under SCCs + MedArc standard contract clauses.
- Location: DataWeave (Ireland, eu-west-1), GeoPulse (US East, us-east-1).

If you need more detail (SCC copy, encryption-at-rest proof, or DataWeave/GeoPulse SOC2 snapshot) let us know and we will provide it. We also included a proposed limited-scope amendment to the subprocessor clause (redline) for your review.

Thanks,
Alicia Turner
Head of Security Operations
MedArc Systems

Alicia —

Thanks for the early notice and for sending the roster and DPIA summary. A few items our compliance and legal teams need in order to sign off on the onward transfer to GeoPulse (US) and DataWeave (IE):

1) Confirm whether any hashed identifiers can be reversed or linked to raw prompt content under your retention/processing flows. We need an assurance that the hashed request IDs are not reversible.
2) Provide a copy of the executed SCCs that will cover transfers to the US (GeoPulse). If SCCs are already in place please attach or provide a drive link.
3) For GeoPulse (US) — we need their most recent SOC 2 Type II report or an attestation. For DataWeave (IE) — confirm SOC/ISO status.
4) Clarify the precise fields included in the telemetry export (sample CSV header is fine).
5) Redline to the subprocessor clause: we will likely need a 30-day notification period for any future downstream changes and an explicit prohibition on forwarding any raw textual content.

We're treating this as a limited-scope subprocessor permission request. Please send the evidentiary docs and indicate whether MedArc can execute our standard limited subprocessor addendum (I can share a DocuSign link) that includes the 30-day notice and data handling constraints.

Cc'ing our contracts and privacy leads (Marissa and Rishi) to expedite review.

Best,

- SCCs: attached are signed SCCs covering GeoPulse transfers (medarc_sccs_geopulse_signed.pdf) and an internal certificate of execution.
- SOC2/ISO: GeoPulse provided a SOC2 attestation (redacted) — file geopulse_soc2_attestation.pdf attached. DataWeave provided an ISO27001 certificate copy.
- Telemetry fields: sample header included in medarc_vendor_roster_20261206.csv; we also included a sample export row.
- Contract redline: see medarc_subproc_terms_redline.docx. We are amenable to the 30-day notification, but request a 14-day operational window for critical security patches that must be applied by downstream processors. If acceptable we can reflect that in the DocuSign amendment.
